examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

meanings.note: 'взять на работу' = to give someone a job
'взять на работу' = to give someone a job

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: В гости = for a visit. Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common masculine noun meaning 'guest, visitor' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Клавдия Викторовна, к вам гости! Па-пам!
examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna, you have visitors! Ta-da!

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Disbelief. Core Russian part meaning 'yes' in everyday speech.
From двор (courtyard). Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'janitor, street sweeper, caretaker' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: In the morning the janitor works in the courtyard.

examples.text: Нормально у вас тут, просторно. И маскировка хорошая, на дворников похожи.
examples.trans: It's nice in here, roomy. And good disguises—you look like janitors.

meanings.note: на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: About people. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('kind; good').
in greetings: добрый день, добрый вечер

meanings.note: в долгу не остаться = to repay a favour

examples.trans: Help me! I'll pay you back, I promise.

meanings.note: A job title, e.g. boss, director. Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'post, position' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: If you change your mind, come back. The job is waiting.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'писать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to finish writing'.

examples.trans: Could you write at the top who it is for?

examples.text: На кухне никто не хочет дописать без причины.
examples.trans: In the kitchen nobody wants to finish writing without a reason.

related.gloss: not to to finish writing (negated infinitive)

meanings.note: Звать на помощь = to call for help. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to call', paired with 'позвать'.
как тебя зовут? = what's your name? меня зовут ... = my name is ...
